reason: Public copy on category hubs and /top pages in this repo had four misses in one session: copy written before asking about antislop (CLAUDE.md requires asking first, asked only at the end), passive "Opini dikumpulkan ... Yang dinilai" text the user had to get reworked, a new unconditional link to a noindex /top/{slug} page, and a pure-text change shipped with no test. Class-level rule for all public copy in resources/js/pages, so the next copy task starts from these constraints.

Implementation of sponsor form copy and helper text went ahead without the antislop question; it was only raised at the end, which this skill already calls a miss. The miss repeated mid-implementation because user said "lanjut implementasi". Extend trigger to UI labels and helper text and make the ask apply mid-task too.

Polish pass on public homepage copy showed en-dash ranges and middle-dot joiners read as AI-generated styling. Indonesian copy needs word-form ranges, and metadata needs split elements. The rule is missing from public-page-copy.

Theme labels rendered on public pages included generic and self-contradicting pairs ("Kualitas mobil bagus" and "Kualitas mobil jelek" on the same entity). The filter now lives in PublicCopyGuard::publishableThemes(); the copy skill must say so, or a later view re-implements it and the entity page and /banding drift apart.

Product FAQ and meta answered "masih worth it?" with opinion counts and percentages that had no period, and numbers were not rounded consistently. Every count needs its window, and the same rounded numbers must be reused across meta, FAQ and cards.

Renaming a theme label (display_label) left the old term in the slug, which still appears in the page's embedded JSON, so a raw grep reported a false leftover. Verification must read visible text and the h1/title, and the rename must keep slug and aliases so matching does not break.

The final lint for public copy scanned only en dash and middle dot. The episode's check also searched em dash, and the em-dash rule (antislop) applies to the same public text. Adding it to the existing end-of-task scan keeps the two lists in step.

Stale instruction superseded by the user's explicit correction in this episode: the user said not to ask whether antislop applies and to apply it while writing. Keeping the old "ask first" line would make the skill contradict the user. Note: the project CLAUDE.md still says "ask the user when antislop applies"; that file cannot be changed by a skill intent and needs a user-side edit to fully reconcile.
